answer: Before a payout, a claimant files a pulse log: thirty signed work receipts spread over thirty days at odd hours, each hashed publicly, the payout held in a haven vault till then. The desk verifies the spacing within a day. A real pulse is uneven; a farmed one beats like a metronome. A too-regular pulse voids the claim and bars the identity a week. One honest worker already holds a month of receipts; 1,000 fakes would need 30,000. One farm stamped five hundred receipts in one night across the tundra; every pulse beat at the same minute, and the desk voided them all.
